questions.scenario: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between artificial intelligence, machine learning and deep learning?
options: Deep learning is a subset of machine learning, which is a subset of artificial intelligence
Artificial intelligence is a subset of deep learning
Machine learning and artificial intelligence are unrelated
Deep learning is broader than artificial intelligence
questions.explain: AI is the widest field, machine learning sits within it, and deep learning sits within machine learning. Generative AI in turn sits within deep learning.

questions.scenario: A company has historical data labelled with the outcome it wants to predict. Which learning approach applies?
questions.explain: Labelled examples showing the correct answer define supervised learning. Unsupervised learning finds structure in unlabelled data, and reinforcement learning uses rewards.

questions.scenario: Which AWS service transcribes recorded audio into text?
questions.explain: Transcribe converts speech to text. Polly performs the reverse, generating speech from text — remember Polly as the parrot that speaks.

questions.scenario: Which AWS service detects objects, scenes and faces in images and video?
questions.explain: Rekognition analyses images and video. Textract extracts text from scanned documents, and Comprehend analyses the meaning of text.

questions.scenario: Which inference type is most cost-effective for scoring a large batch of records overnight?
questions.explain: Batch inference processes large volumes at once with results available later, avoiding the cost of a continuously running real-time endpoint.

questions.scenario: Which metric measures the proportion of genuine positive cases that a model successfully identified?
questions.explain: Recall measures how many real positive cases were caught, so it matters most when missing a case is costly — disease screening or fraud detection.

questions.scenario: Which AWS service produces time-series forecasts such as future product demand?
questions.explain: Forecast is the managed time-series forecasting service. Personalize produces recommendations and Fraud Detector identifies fraudulent activity.

questions.scenario: Which task is an example of regression rather than classification?
options: Deciding whether an email is spam
Identifying the language of a document
Detecting whether an image contains a cat
questions.explain: Regression predicts a continuous numeric value such as price. The other three assign a discrete category, which is classification.

questions.scenario: When is a machine learning solution generally NOT appropriate?
options: When a guaranteed, exact outcome defined by fixed rules is required
When large volumes of historical data exist
When patterns are too complex to code by hand
When predictions can tolerate some uncertainty
questions.explain: ML produces probabilistic predictions, not guarantees. Where an exact outcome is defined by clear rules, conventional deterministic logic is the correct tool — a point the exam guide makes explicitly.

questions.scenario: Which AWS service extracts text, forms and tables from scanned documents?
questions.explain: Textract extracts structured content from scanned documents and forms. Comprehend then analyses the meaning of text that already exists in digital form.

questions.scenario: What does MLOps refer to?
options: Applying repeatable, monitored engineering practices to machine learning systems
A type of neural network architecture
A billing model for AI services
A method of encrypting training data
questions.explain: MLOps covers experimentation, repeatable processes, scalable systems, monitoring and retraining — engineering discipline applied to ML rather than a model type.

questions.scenario: Which AWS service provides recommendations such as 'customers who bought this also bought'?
questions.explain: Personalize is the managed recommendation service. Kendra provides intelligent enterprise search, which is a different retrieval problem.

questions.scenario: Which TWO characteristics describe unstructured data?
options: Free-text documents with no predefined schema
Rows and columns in a relational table
A CSV file with fixed headers
questions.explain: Free text, images and audio have no predefined schema and are unstructured. Tables, CSVs with fixed headers and normalised schemas all impose structure.

questions.scenario: Which AWS service provides API access to foundation models from several providers without managing infrastructure?
questions.explain: Bedrock provides serverless API access to foundation models. SageMaker AI is the platform for building and training your own models, requiring far more expertise.

questions.scenario: What is a token in the context of a large language model?
options: A small unit of text, roughly three-quarters of a word
questions.explain: Tokens are the units of text models read and generate, and are the unit of billing. The security meaning of 'token' is unrelated in this context.

questions.scenario: Which term describes a model producing confident but factually incorrect output?
questions.explain: Hallucination is confident falsehood and is generative AI's best-known weakness. Overfitting and underfitting are training problems, and drift is degradation over time.

questions.scenario: What are embeddings used for in a generative AI application?
options: Representing text as vectors so semantically similar items are numerically close
questions.explain: Embeddings turn text into vectors where similar meanings are close together, which is what makes semantic search and retrieval-augmented generation possible.

questions.scenario: A team notices its Amazon Bedrock costs rising sharply after adding a long standing instruction to every request. Which change would MOST directly reduce this cost?
options: Shorten the repeated instruction or enable prompt caching
Switch the application to a different AWS Region
Add more few-shot examples to the prompt
questions.explain: Bedrock bills per token in both directions, so a long instruction repeated on every request is charged every time. Shortening it or caching the repeated portion cuts cost directly. Adding examples increases tokens, temperature has no cost effect, and Region choice does not change token pricing.

questions.scenario: What does 'multi-modal' mean when applied to a foundation model?
options: It can process more than one type of data, such as text and images
It runs in more than one Region
questions.explain: Multi-modal means handling several data types. Modality refers to the kind of data — text, image, audio — not deployment or pricing.

questions.scenario: Which AWS capability lets a foundation model invoke tools and complete multi-step tasks?
questions.explain: Agents let a model plan and call external tools across multiple steps. Guardrails enforces content safety, a different function.

questions.scenario: What role does the Model Context Protocol (MCP) play in agentic AI?
options: It provides a standard way for agents to connect to external systems and tools
questions.explain: MCP standardises how agents connect to external systems and tools, and is named explicitly in the AIF-C01 exam guide.

questions.scenario: Which is a recognised disadvantage of generative AI systems?
options: Nondeterminism — the same prompt can produce different outputs
questions.explain: Nondeterminism means identical prompts can yield different responses, which complicates testing. It is listed alongside hallucination and limited interpretability.

questions.scenario: Which AWS service is an AI-powered assistant for business and development questions?
questions.explain: Amazon Q is AWS's AI assistant for business users and developers. The others are speech synthesis, data discovery and graph database services.

questions.scenario: What does 'chunking' refer to when preparing documents for retrieval?
options: Splitting documents into smaller pieces that can be embedded and retrieved
questions.explain: Chunking splits large documents into retrievable pieces before embedding. Chunk size affects retrieval quality directly — too large returns noise, too small loses context.

questions.scenario: Which model family is typically used to generate images?
questions.explain: Diffusion models generate images, whereas transformer-based LLMs generate text. Both are foundation model families named in the exam guide.

questions.scenario: Which business metric would best indicate that a generative AI assistant is delivering value?
options: Task completion rate and user satisfaction
Size of the model in gigabytes
questions.explain: Business alignment is measured by outcomes such as task completion rate, user satisfaction, cost per interaction and ROI. The other options are technical inputs.

questions.scenario: Which stage of the foundation model lifecycle immediately follows evaluation?
questions.explain: The lifecycle runs data selection, model selection, pre-training, fine-tuning, evaluation, deployment, then feedback. Deployment follows evaluation.

questions.scenario: What is the main advantage of a smaller foundation model over a larger one?
options: Lower latency and lower cost per request
questions.explain: Smaller models generally respond faster and cost less, which matters for latency-sensitive or high-volume applications. They do not eliminate bias or the need for evaluation.

questions.scenario: Which TWO factors should be considered when selecting a foundation model for a production application?
options: The number of Availability Zones in the Region
The colour scheme of the console
questions.explain: Cost, latency, modality, model size, customisability and language support are the documented selection criteria. Availability Zone count, support plan and console appearance are irrelevant to model choice.

questions.scenario: A company needs a chatbot to answer from internal documents that change daily, with citations. Which approach?
questions.explain: Daily changes plus a citation requirement both point to RAG, which retrieves live documents at query time. Fine-tuning cannot cite sources and would need daily repetition.

questions.scenario: Which customisation approach changes a model's writing style and tone permanently?
questions.explain: Fine-tuning retrains the model, changing how it writes. RAG supplies information without altering the model. Remember: RAG changes what it knows, fine-tuning changes how it speaks.

questions.scenario: Which inference parameter primarily controls randomness in generated output?
questions.explain: Temperature governs randomness — low values give consistent output, high values more variety. Max tokens limits length and the context window limits input size.

questions.scenario: Which prompting technique supplies several worked examples within the prompt?
questions.explain: Few-shot prompting includes several examples to guide format and style. Zero-shot supplies none and chain-of-thought requests step-by-step reasoning.

questions.scenario: Which technique most improves accuracy on multi-step reasoning problems?
questions.explain: Chain-of-thought elicits intermediate reasoning steps, substantially improving multi-step arithmetic and logic. Higher temperature adds randomness rather than rigour.

questions.scenario: Which metric is used to evaluate the quality of machine-generated summaries?
questions.explain: ROUGE evaluates summarisation and BLEU evaluates translation. Memorising that pairing answers a recurring exam question.

questions.scenario: Which metric evaluates machine translation quality?
questions.explain: BLEU is the translation metric; ROUGE is for summarisation. Recall and accuracy are classification metrics rather than generation metrics.

questions.scenario: Which AWS feature provides managed retrieval-augmented generation without building the pipeline yourself?
questions.explain: Knowledge Bases is AWS's managed RAG implementation, handling chunking, embedding and retrieval. Prompt Management stores and versions prompts instead.

questions.scenario: Which AWS service can store vector embeddings for a retrieval application?
questions.explain: OpenSearch Service supports vector search, as do Aurora, Neptune and RDS for PostgreSQL. Glacier is archival storage and CloudTrail is an audit log.

questions.scenario: A company wants to reduce inference cost while retaining most of a large model's capability. Which technique?
questions.explain: Distillation produces a smaller, cheaper model approximating a larger one. Extra examples and a wider context window both increase token usage and therefore cost.

questions.scenario: Which approach supplies examples at inference time without changing the model's weights?
questions.explain: In-context learning — zero-, one- and few-shot prompting — guides the model through the prompt alone. The other approaches all modify the model itself.

questions.scenario: Which technique reduces cost when a long, unchanging instruction is sent with every request?
questions.explain: Prompt caching reuses the repeated portion of a prompt, reducing both cost and latency for requests that share a long preamble.

questions.scenario: Which evaluation approach uses one language model to grade another's output?
questions.explain: LLM-as-a-judge scales evaluation by having a model assess responses. Human evaluation is more reliable for subjective quality but does not scale as well.

questions.scenario: What is the purpose of reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF)?
options: Aligning model behaviour with human preferences
Compressing the model for faster inference
questions.explain: RLHF uses human preference judgements to make model behaviour more helpful and aligned. Compression is distillation, a separate technique.

questions.scenario: Which characteristic should training data have when fine-tuning a model for a specialist domain?
options: Curated, representative and well governed with documented provenance
As large as possible regardless of quality
Drawn from a single narrow source
questions.explain: Fine-tuning quality depends on curated, representative, governed data. Sheer volume does not compensate for poor or unrepresentative content.

questions.scenario: A RAG application returns irrelevant passages. Which change is most likely to help?
options: Improving how documents are chunked and embedded
questions.explain: Retrieval quality depends on chunking and embedding — poor chunking retrieves the wrong passages. Temperature and token limits affect generation, not retrieval.

questions.scenario: Which Amazon Bedrock capability compares foundation models against defined criteria?
questions.explain: Model Evaluation compares models using automatic metrics and human review. Ground Truth labels data and Guardrails filters content.

questions.scenario: Which TWO approaches supply a model with current, organisation-specific information at query time?
options: Retrieval Augmented Generation over a document store
questions.explain: RAG and its managed AWS implementation, Knowledge Bases, both retrieve current organisational content at query time. Temperature, token limits and batch size do not add information.

questions.scenario: Which AWS service detects bias in a model and explains individual predictions?
questions.explain: Clarify covers both bias detection across groups and explainability of individual predictions. Guardrails is Bedrock's content-safety feature, not a fairness auditor.

questions.scenario: Which capability blocks a generative AI application from discussing prohibited topics?
questions.explain: Guardrails supports denied topics and harmful content filtering. Clarify measures fairness and explainability, which is a different concern.

questions.scenario: What is the most likely root cause when a model consistently disadvantages one demographic group?
options: Bias present in the training data
A temperature setting that is too low
questions.explain: Models reproduce patterns in their training data, so demographic unfairness almost always originates there. Inference settings and compute do not create it.

questions.scenario: Which AWS capability documents a model's intended use, training data and limitations?
questions.explain: Model Cards provide transparency documentation. Clarify provides explainability — why a decision was made — which the exam treats as distinct from transparency.

questions.scenario: Which service routes low-confidence predictions to human reviewers?
questions.explain: A2I inserts human review into workflows for uncertain or high-risk predictions, implementing the human-in-the-loop principle.

questions.scenario: Which term describes a model that memorises its training data and generalises poorly?
questions.explain: Overfitting means excellent training performance but poor results on new data. Underfitting means the model learned too little and performs poorly everywhere.

questions.scenario: Which legal risk is specifically associated with generative AI output?
questions.explain: IP infringement is among the GenAI legal risks the exam guide names, alongside biased outputs, hallucinations and loss of customer trust.

questions.scenario: Six months after deployment, a fraud model's accuracy has fallen because customer behaviour has shifted. What is this phenomenon called?
questions.explain: Drift is degradation after deployment as real-world data diverges from the training data, and is detected with SageMaker Model Monitor. Overfitting is a training-time fault, visible before deployment rather than months later.

questions.scenario: Which responsible AI characteristic describes a model performing reliably under unexpected or adversarial input?
questions.explain: Robustness means holding up under difficult or adversarial conditions, and is listed alongside fairness, inclusivity, safety and veracity.

questions.scenario: A user embeds hidden instructions in a chatbot message to override its original instructions. What is this attack called?
questions.explain: Prompt injection hijacks a model through crafted input — the AI equivalent of SQL injection. Defences are input validation, output filtering and Guardrails.

questions.scenario: A company must confirm that no customer national identity numbers have been uploaded into the S3 bucket used to build its training dataset. Which service should it use?
questions.explain: Macie scans S3 and classifies sensitive data such as national identity numbers and other PII. Config tracks resource configuration rather than object contents, and Audit Manager collects audit evidence rather than scanning data.

questions.scenario: Which service provides an audit trail of API calls made against Amazon Bedrock?
questions.explain: CloudTrail records who called which API and when. CloudWatch monitors performance metrics, and Config records resource configuration state.

questions.scenario: Which approach ensures traffic to AWS AI services does not traverse the public internet?
questions.explain: PrivateLink keeps traffic on the AWS network. CloudFront and Global Accelerator both improve delivery performance but still involve the public internet.

questions.scenario: Under the shared responsibility model, who is responsible for the prompts and data submitted to a foundation model?
questions.explain: Customer data and prompts are always the customer's responsibility. AWS secures the infrastructure, the service and the model itself.

questions.scenario: Which combination best reduces hallucinations in a production GenAI application?
options: RAG grounding together with output validation
Raising the temperature and shortening prompts
Using a larger context window only
questions.explain: Grounding answers in real sources and validating output before delivery is the documented approach. Temperature changes randomness and does not improve factual accuracy.

questions.scenario: Which governance requirement determines which country an organisation's training data may be stored in?
questions.explain: Data residency dictates the geographic location where data may be held, usually for legal reasons. It is a governance constraint rather than a technical setting.

questions.scenario: Which service helps collect evidence continuously to support compliance audits?
questions.explain: Audit Manager continuously collects evidence for your own audits. Artifact provides AWS's own compliance reports, which is the complementary half.

questions.scenario: Which practice documents where training data originated and how it has been transformed?
questions.explain: Data lineage and cataloging record provenance and transformations, supporting governance and auditability. The other options are performance or cost techniques.
